nodes.prompt: In tools/agent-harness, `harness stats --days <n>` does `Number(opt('days') ?? 30)` in bin/harness.ts, so `--days abc` or `--days -3` silently produces a NaN/negative window and prints garbage stats. Make it reject anything that is not a positive integer via the existing usage() helper (exit code 2, message naming --days). Add tests to test/cli.test.ts that run the CLI (follow the existing `run([...])` helper there) for --days abc, --days 0, --days -3 (exit 2) and --days 7 (exit 0). Write the failing tests first, watch them fail, then fix. Keep the change minimal.

contract.goal: harness stats rejects a non-positive-integer --days with exit 2; valid --days still works

verify.name: stats rejects NaN
cmd: cd tools/agent-harness && AGENT_HARNESS_DB=$(mktemp -d)/l.db bun run bin/harness.ts stats --days abc; test $? -eq 2

nodes.prompt: In tools/agent-harness/src/notify.ts, readVar() parses the Telegram token out of an env file but ignores lines written as `export TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN=...`, so a user who writes the file that way silently gets no notifications. Make readVar accept an optional leading `export ` (and surrounding whitespace), keep quote stripping, and ignore comment lines. Put the tests in a NEW file test/notify.test.ts (do not edit test/cli.test.ts — another agent owns it right now): export form, plain form, quoted, commented-out line not used. Write the failing tests first, watch them fail, then fix. Export readVar if you need to test it directly.

contract.goal: notify.ts reads TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN from `export KEY=v` lines as well as `KEY=v`, ignoring comments
